correctness.rationale: Exact-length walks reach precisely the positions at compatible parity and distance at most t. The two target-parity distance-to-support maxima differ by one because distance changes by at most one across an edge and has opposite parities on the two classes. First saturation is therefore R−1; full and empty target classes stay full and empty while the classes swap. This yields the four recurrent states and the maximum of the two support clocks. An antipodal singleton is the only way to have R=d; a nonsingleton with R=d−1 lies in a Hamming-1 star. Each qualifying pair lies in two stars and a larger support lies in just one, giving U and both max-clock counts. A fresh cycle census on all 256 d=3 states gave (4,140,112); exhaustive parity censuses gave (N,U)=(4,10),(8,64),(16,336) for d=3,4,5. For the random claim, ordered k-tuples with an overlapping neighborhood number O_k(2^{d(k−1)}d²), and the union of their neighborhoods loses at most 2 binom(k,2) from kd. Their contribution is o(1); the disjoint tuples give the Poisson factorial moments. At two steps each predecessor set has size 1+binom(d,2); a union bound suffices. Empty seed parity classes and initial periodicity are negligible. For fixed p below or above 1/2, the second-moment or first-moment bound respectively gives the stated law. Inspected the three frozen checkers without executing them.
